state.claim: McDonald’s take down American flags at their fast-food restaurants in support of Black Lives Matter and antifa (an umbrella term for far-left anti-fascism groups).

candidates.quote: The McDonald's message says nothing about antifa, a loosely linked group of anti-fascist activists who monitor white supremacists and neo-Nazis. Antifa and Black Lives Matter are two separate movements that sometimes are conflated by opponents on the right.
We rate this claim as FALSE, based on the company's statement and our research. There has been no nationwide removal of U.S. flags at McDonald's restaurants.
Sep 17, 2020 — A McDonald's USA spokesperson confirmed this claim is not true and there is no coordinated effort to remove American flags from its restaurants .

In a statement to FactCheck.org, McDonald’s USA stated that the company “unequivocally stands behind the need for equality and social justice, and these rumors [about the American flag] are not true.”

It’s unclear why the social media posts have targeted McDonald’s, but there is no evidence for the claim that the fast-food chain removed American flags in support of Black Lives Matter and antifa. And the company has said the accusation is false.
VERDICT False. McDonald's confirmed to Reuters that it has not removed U.S. flags to show support for Antifa and Black Lives Matter.

S1.title: McDonald's US flags have not been removed for BLM, antifa
S1.retrieval_query: Did any specific McDonald's restaurants actually remove American flags, and is there photographic, video, or documentary evidence identifying the locations and dates involved?

passages.P1: # Fact check: McDonald's US flags have not been removed for BLM and antifa
passages.P2: ## The claim: McDonald's has a nationwide edict related to flags and Black Lives Matter
passages.P3: A Facebook post from Sept. 17 calls for a boycott of the world's largest restaurant chain.
passages.P4: "McDonald's removes their American flags in support of Antifa & BLM nationwide," it reads. The post generated 5,100 shares and such comments as: "They are showing their colors!" and "Mcdonalds is goin down!"
passages.P5: The post mimics a Twitter post from Sept. 15, making the same claim. It had nearly 7,000 retweets and 6,000 likes. In one retweet, a Twitter user wrote: "Done with them. America made McDonald', and we will un-make them."
passages.P6: The person or persons behind the Facebook post and tweet have not responded to a request for comment.
passages.P8: Following the death of George Floyd, McDonald's – as did many companies – issued a statement in support of Black Lives Matter, the movement with a mission to "eradicate white supremacy and build local power to intervene in violence inflicted on Black communities by the state and vigilantes."
passages.P9: The McDonald's tribute names George Floyd, Botham Jean, Michael Brown and other unarmed Black men and women who have been killed, and continues, in part:
passages.P11: We see them in our crew members.
passages.P12: We see them in our franchisees.
passages.P13: "And this is why the entire McDonald’s family grieves.
passages.P14: It’s why we stand for them and any other
passages.P15: victims of systemic oppression and violence."
passages.P16: McDonald's announced a donation to the National Urban League and the NAACP, and closed the message by stating: "Black lives matter."
passages.P17: The McDonald's message says nothing about antifa, a loosely linked group of anti-fascist activists who monitor white supremacists and neo-Nazis. Antifa and Black Lives Matter are two separate movements that sometimes are conflated by opponents on the right.
passages.P18: Not all McDonald's have flags. But on Monday, a reporter found one in New Smyrna Beach, Florida, flying the U.S. flag at half-staff in honor of Supreme Court Justice Ruth Bader Ginsburg, who died on Friday.
passages.P19: In an email to the USA TODAY Network, McDonald's USA responded: "McDonald's unequivocally stands behind the need for equality and social justice, and these rumors are not true."
passages.P21: We rate this claim as FALSE, based on the company's statement and our research. There has been no nationwide removal of U.S. flags at McDonald's restaurants.

passages.P2: Social media posts — without evidence — have accused McDonald’s of taking down American flags in support of Black Lives Matter and antifa. The company says that is “not true.”
passages.P4: McDonald’s has recently faced backlash after social media posts accused the company of taking down American flags at their fast-food restaurants in support of Black Lives Matter and antifa, an umbrella term for far-left anti-fascism groups. The rumor appears to have originated from a Sept. 15 tweet by user @Ron4Trump38, and has since spread to Facebook with the call to action “#boycottMcDonalds.” The @Ron4Trump38 account is a self-identified “[t]ruther,” a title synonymous with conspiracy theorists.
passages.P5: In a statement to FactCheck.org, McDonald’s USA stated that the company “unequivocally stands behind the need for equality and social justice, and these rumors [about the American flag] are not true.”
passages.P6: On June 3, McDonald’s tweeted a short clip listing the names of Black victims of police brutality. Among other messages, the clip stated “we stand for them and any other victims of systemic oppression and violence,” and the company announced it would be donating $1 million to the National Urban League and the NAACP. However, the post didn’t mention Black Lives Matter or antifa.
passages.P7: It’s unclear why the social media posts have targeted McDonald’s, but there is no evidence for the claim that the fast-food chain removed American flags in support of Black Lives Matter and antifa. And the company has said the accusation is false.
passages.P8: *Editor’s note: FactCheck.org is one of several organizations**working with Facebook**to debunk misinformation shared on social media. Our previous stories can be found here.*
passages.P10: Ellingson, Doug. “McDonald’s removes their American flags in support of Antifa & BLM nationwide. #boycottMcDonalds.” Facebook. 16 Sep 2020.
passages.P11: Hanbury, Mary. “McDonald’s, Amazon, H&M and more donate millions of dollars to racial justice organizations.” Business Insider. 4 Jun 2020.
passages.P12: McDonald’s (@McDonalds). “They were one of us: Trayvon Martin. Michael Brown. Alton Sterling. Botham Jean. Atatiana Jefferson. Ahmaud Arbery. George Floyd.” Twitter. 3 Jun 2020.
passages.P13: McDonald’s USA. Email sent to FactCheck.org. 21 Sep 2020.
passages.P14: Truther, Ron R (@Ron4Trump38). “I am a True Truther. I am also a free spirit (not a Repub or a Dem). Follow me and I’ll follow you. Maybe we have stuff in common. I do it all! #MAGA.” Twitter. Accessed, 24 Sep 2020.
passages.P15: Truther, Ron R (@Ron4Trump38). “McDonald’s removes their American flags in support of Antifa & BLM nationwide.” Twitter. 15 Sep 2020.
